objectives.statement: Explain how Bayes' theorem combines a prior and a likelihood to infer hidden states from observations.
Formulate a linear-Gaussian generative model and compare exact grid Bayesian inference, precision-weighted posteriors, and MLE or MAP point estimates.
Distinguish parameter learning from hidden-state inference across Bayesian linear regression, multivariate linear-Gaussian systems, and expectation-maximization in factor analysis.
Derive variational free energy as an upper bound on surprisal and minimize it with mean-field CAVI and fixed-form variational inference to approximate a posterior.
Derive predictive-coding recognition dynamics as gradient descent on free energy using precision-weighted prediction errors in single-layer and hierarchical models.
Track dynamic hidden states online with generalized filtering and explain how generalized coordinates of motion and precision coupling reduce tracking lag.
Couple perception and action under a single variational free-energy objective so continuous control steers hidden states toward a preferred set-point.

units.title: Chapter 8 — Learning, attention, and hierarchical models

objectives.statement: Combine fast hidden-state perception with slow parameter learning, log-precision attention updates, and two-layer hierarchical message passing under one free-energy objective.
Construct a discrete POMDP generative model with A, B, C, and D arrays to infer hidden states and select policies by minimizing expected free energy.

units.title: Chapter 10 — Learning and extensions in POMDPs

objectives.statement: Update POMDP parameters through Dirichlet concentration counts and extend discrete active inference with policy precision, habits, factorial state factors, and hierarchical depth.
Compare alternate free-energy planning objectives and apply sophisticated lookahead, time-dependent preferences, parameter forgetting, and structure learning in discrete planning.

units.title: Chapter 12 — Factor graphs and message passing

objectives.statement: Formulate discrete active inference as local factor-graph message passing across sum-product smoothing, variational message passing, and hybrid continuous-discrete bridges.
Apply active-inference belief updating and preference-driven control to robotics navigation, fault-tolerant actuation, and social intention inference.

units.title: Chapter 14 — Bayesian mechanics and Markov blankets

objectives.statement: Relate ergodic occupancy density, entropy and free-energy bounds, viability thresholds, and Markov-blanket partitions to Bayesian mechanics.

glossary.definition: A generative model is the agent's internal representation of the environment, expressed as the joint distribution `p(x, y) = p(y | x) p(x)` over hidden states `x` and observations `y`.
